name: Data Structures & Algorithms Foundations Track
description: Master algorithmic problem solving, Big-O time and space complexity analysis, dynamic arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, binary search, sorting algorithms, trees, and graph algorithms.
whatYouLearn: Analyze time and space complexities using asymptotic Big-O notation
Implement fundamental linear data structures: Stacks, Queues, Linked Lists
Master divide-and-conquer searching and sorting algorithms
Construct non-linear structures: Binary Search Trees (BST) and Heaps
Apply Graph traversal algorithms (BFS and DFS)
Build a production Algorithm Visualizer & Execution Engine
prerequisites: Programming Fundamentals in JavaScript, Python, or C++

exercises.title: Big-O Asymptotic Complexity Analysis
exercises.description: Calculate Big-O time complexities (O(1), O(log N), O(N), O(N log N), O(N^2)).
exercises.theory: Big-O notation describes upper-bound execution time or memory space growth rate as input size N approaches infinity.
exercises.objective: Identify and demonstrate O(1) constant time vs O(N) linear time functions.
exercises.initialCode: // Identify O(1) constant vs O(N) linear operations
requirements: Demonstrate O(1) constant array indexing
Demonstrate O(N) linear search traversal loop
hints: O(1) execution duration does not depend on array size N

exercises.title: Two-Pointer Technique
exercises.description: Solve array problems in linear O(N) time using converging two-pointer references.
exercises.theory: The two-pointer technique uses left and right index pointers moving towards each other to solve array searching problems in linear time.
exercises.objective: Find a target sum pair in a sorted array using two pointers.
requirements: Initialize left = 0 and right = arr.length - 1
Converge pointers inside while (left < right) loop
Achieve O(N) time complexity and O(1) extra space
hints: If currentSum < target, increment left pointer to increase sum
exercises.codeExample: while (l < r) { if (arr[l] + arr[r] === target) return [l, r]; }

exercises.title: Sliding Window Pattern
exercises.description: Find maximum subarray sum of fixed size K using the Sliding Window pattern.
exercises.theory: The sliding window pattern reuses overlapping subarray computations to reduce O(N * K) brute force algorithms into linear O(N) time.
exercises.objective: Calculate maximum sum of contiguous subarray of size K.
requirements: Calculate initial K elements sum
Slide window by adding new element arr[i] and subtracting outgoing element arr[i - k]
Achieve O(N) linear time complexity
hints: Subtracting the leaving element avoids re-summing all elements inside the window

exercises.title: Stack Data Structure (LIFO - Last In First Out)
exercises.description: Implement a Stack with push, pop, peek, and isEmpty methods.
exercises.theory: A Stack follows Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) ordering. Elements are added to and removed from the top.
exercises.objective: Build a Stack class and solve a valid parentheses matching problem.
requirements: Implement Stack class with LIFO methods
Use Stack to validate balanced parentheses string
hints: Popping mismatched bracket from stack indicates invalid string
exercises.codeExample: class Stack { push(x) { this.items.push(x); } pop() { return this.items.pop(); } }

exercises.title: Queue Data Structure (FIFO - First In First Out)
exercises.description: Implement a Queue with enqueue, dequeue, and peek methods.
exercises.theory: A Queue operates on First-In-First-Out (FIFO) ordering. Items enter at the back (enqueue) and exit from the front (dequeue).
exercises.objective: Build a Queue class for task processing.
requirements: Implement O(1) Queue with object storage and head/tail pointers
Demonstrate enqueue and dequeue operations
hints: Using object dictionary with head/tail pointers achieves O(1) dequeue operations, avoiding array shift() O(N) cost

exercises.title: Singly Linked List Implementation
exercises.description: Build a Singly Linked List with append, prepend, and traversal methods.
exercises.theory: A Linked List is a linear chain of nodes containing value and next pointer references.
exercises.objective: Build a Singly Linked List class.
requirements: Define Node class with val and next fields
Implement LinkedList class with prepend and toArray methods
hints: Prepending to a linked list takes O(1) constant time
exercises.codeExample: class Node { constructor(v) { this.val = v; this.next = null; } }

exercises.title: Reversing a Singly Linked List
exercises.description: Reverse a Singly Linked List in O(N) time and O(1) space.
exercises.theory: Reversing a linked list involves re-pointing each node's next reference to its preceding node during traversal.
exercises.objective: Write a reverseLinkedList function.
requirements: Traverse linked list using prev, curr, and nextTemp pointers
Reverse node.next references in O(N) time and O(1) space
hints: Save curr.next into temporary variable before overwriting curr.next = prev
exercises.codeExample: while (curr) { let next = curr.next; curr.next = prev; prev = curr; curr = next; }

exercises.title: Binary Search Algorithm (O(log N))
exercises.description: Implement Binary Search on a sorted array in O(log N) time complexity.
exercises.theory: Binary Search cuts search space in half repeatedly on sorted arrays, achieving logarithmic O(log N) efficiency.
exercises.objective: Write Binary Search function returning target index.
requirements: Calculate mid = Math.floor(left + (right - left) / 2)
Halve search bounds in while (left <= right) loop
Achieve O(log N) logarithmic time complexity
hints: Math.floor(left + (right - left) / 2) prevents potential integer overflow

exercises.title: Bubble Sort & Selection Sort
exercises.description: Implement fundamental quadratic O(N^2) sorting algorithms.
exercises.theory: Bubble Sort repeatedly swaps adjacent out-of-order elements until array is sorted, running in O(N^2) quadratic time.
exercises.objective: Write in-place Bubble Sort function.
requirements: Use nested loops to swap adjacent elements
Add swapped flag early exit optimization
hints: Early exit when no swaps occur optimizes best-case time to O(N)

exercises.title: Merge Sort (Divide & Conquer O(N log N))
exercises.description: Implement recursive Merge Sort with divide-and-conquer strategy.
exercises.theory: Merge Sort recursively splits arrays into halves (divide) and merges sorted sub-arrays back together (conquer) in guaranteed O(N log N) time.
exercises.objective: Write recursive mergeSort and helper merge functions.
requirements: Base case: return arr if arr.length <= 1
Split array at mid index and recursively sort halves
Merge sorted halves using two pointers
hints: Merge Sort guarantees O(N log N) time complexity in all cases

exercises.title: Quick Sort Algorithm
exercises.description: Implement Quick Sort partitioning around pivot elements.
exercises.theory: Quick Sort selects a pivot element, partitions elements into smaller and larger sub-arrays, and recursively sorts sub-arrays.
exercises.objective: Write Quick Sort partitioning function.
requirements: Select pivot element
Partition array into left (< pivot) and right (>= pivot)
Recursively sort and concatenate [...quickSort(left), pivot, ...quickSort(right)]
hints: Average time complexity of Quick Sort is O(N log N)

exercises.title: Binary Search Tree (BST) Insertion & Lookup
exercises.description: Construct a Binary Search Tree supporting insert and search operations.
exercises.theory: In a BST, left child values are strictly less than node value, and right child values are strictly greater.
exercises.objective: Build TreeNode and BST insert and search methods.
requirements: Define TreeNode with val, left, right
Implement BST insert method enforcing BST property
hints: BST properties guarantee average O(log N) lookup time

exercises.title: Tree Traversals (In-Order, Pre-Order, Post-Order)
exercises.description: Traverse tree nodes recursively in In-Order, Pre-Order, and Post-Order sequences.
exercises.theory: In-Order traversal (Left -> Node -> Right) visits BST nodes in sorted ascending order. Pre-Order is (Node -> Left -> Right). Post-Order is (Left -> Right -> Node).
exercises.objective: Implement inOrderTraversal function.
requirements: Recursively visit left child, process node, and visit right child
Return array of visited node values in sorted order
hints: In-Order traversal on a valid BST always yields sorted ascending values

exercises.title: Breadth-First Search (BFS) Level-Order Traversal
exercises.description: Traverse tree or graph levels using Breadth-First Search (BFS) with a Queue.
exercises.theory: BFS visits nodes level-by-level using a Queue to store candidate nodes at current depth before moving deeper.
exercises.objective: Implement levelOrderTraversal for Binary Tree using a Queue.
requirements: Use Queue to store nodes at active level
Process nodes level-by-level and push child nodes into queue
hints: Capturing levelSize = queue.length at loop start isolates node count per level
exercises.codeExample: const queue = [root]; while (queue.length) { const node = queue.shift(); }

exercises.title: Graph Representation: Adjacency List
exercises.description: Represent directed and undirected graphs using an Adjacency List Map.
exercises.theory: Adjacency Lists map each vertex node key to an array of its neighboring connected vertices.
exercises.objective: Build a Graph class with addVertex and addEdge methods.
requirements: Create Graph class with Map adjacency list
Implement addVertex and addEdge for undirected graph
hints: Undirected graphs add edges in both directions (v1 -> v2 and v2 -> v1)

exercises.title: Graph Traversal: Depth-First Search (DFS)
exercises.description: Traverse graph vertices recursively using Depth-First Search (DFS).
exercises.theory: DFS explores as deep as possible along each branch before backtracking, utilizing a visited set to avoid infinite loops in cyclic graphs.
exercises.objective: Implement DFS graph traversal using Set for visited nodes.
requirements: Use Set to track visited nodes
Recursively traverse neighbor nodes
Return array of visited vertex nodes
hints: Set.has(node) check prevents visiting nodes multiple times in cyclic graphs

exercises.title: Dynamic Programming: Fibonacci & Memoization
exercises.description: Optimize exponential recursive algorithms into linear O(N) time using memoization.
exercises.theory: Dynamic Programming stores solutions to overlapping sub-problems (memoization) to eliminate redundant recursive calculations.
exercises.objective: Build memoized fibonacci function.
requirements: Use memo object parameter to cache sub-problem results
Check n in memo before recursive computation
Reduce time complexity from O(2^N) to linear O(N)
hints: Memoization transforms exponential O(2^N) recursion into linear O(N) time
exercises.codeExample: if (n in memo) return memo[n]; memo[n] = fib(n-1) + fib(n-2);

exercises.title: Priority Queue & Binary Min-Heap
exercises.description: Construct a Binary Min-Heap supporting bubble-up and bubble-down operations.
exercises.theory: Min-Heap is a complete binary tree where parent node value is <= child node values. Top node (index 0) always holds the minimum element.
exercises.objective: Build MinHeap insert and extractMin operations.
requirements: Store heap elements in single array
Calculate parent index Math.floor((idx - 1) / 2)
Implement bubbleUp swapping elements while node < parent
hints: Min-Heap root (index 0) always contains minimum element in O(1) time

exercises.title: Trie Data Structure (Prefix Tree)
exercises.description: Construct a Trie (Prefix Tree) for efficient autocomplete string prefix lookups.
exercises.theory: A Trie stores characters as node branches, enabling prefix searching (startsWith) in O(L) time where L is word length.
exercises.objective: Build Trie insert and startsWith methods.
requirements: Define TrieNode with children object and isWord boolean
Implement insert and startsWith methods
hints: Trie startsWith executes in O(L) time independent of total words stored

exercises.title: Capstone Project: Algorithm Execution & Visualization Engine
exercises.description: Engineer a complete Algorithm Execution Engine featuring Sorting step-by-step state tracking, Binary Search logging, and Execution Benchmarking.
exercises.theory: This capstone project synthesizes core Data Structures and Algorithms: Sorting state step generation, Binary Search, Big-O complexity analysis, and execution benchmarking into a complete Algorithm Visualizer Engine.
exercises.objective: Construct a complete Algorithm Engine module.
exercises.initialCode: // Engineer Algorithm Visualizer & Execution Engine
requirements: Implement generateSortingSteps emitting compare and swap state frames
Implement benchmarkAlgorithm calculating high-resolution duration with performance.now()
hints: Emitting step objects with cloned array state snapshots allows UI components to animate step-by-step sorting progress

references.title: Algorithms (Sedgewick & Wayne)
references.description: Comprehensive reference textbook for computer science data structures and algorithms
